newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovnaft to invest SKK 27 bln by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Slovnaft to invest SKK 27 bln by 2000.

text.p: Slovakia's monopoly oil refiner Slovnaft a.s will invest more than 27 billion crowns into its modernisation by the end of the century, a senior company official said on Monday.
"In comparison, the current value of our assets is 16.5 billion crowns," Slovanaft Deputy Financial Director Dusan Durmis told capital markets conference in Bratislava.
The main investment, some 15 billion crowns, is for Slovnaft's so-called Environmental Fuel Project Apollo (EFPA).
EFPA is a complex of production units for the conversion of heavy oil fractions with a high sulphur content into motor fuels and the production of low-sulphur heating oil, he said.
"This will enable better utilisation of raw materials and the production of lead-free petrol, and will also enable us to lower input of the basic raw material, crude oil," he added.
Turnkey delivery contracts for production units worth $300 million have already been signed with Stork Comprimo VMFN, Fluor Daniel, Mitsubishi Heavy Industry, Chiyoda, Raytheon.

Other projects include expansion of the petrol distribution network, a reforming process with continuous catalyser regeneration, a complex of units for hydro-cracking heavy crude fractions, hydrogen production and sulphur production.
Some Slovak firms will act as construction sub-contractors, Durmis said, but added that Slovnaft was disappointed with the general standard of many Slovak enterprises.

"We regrettably note that based on the negotiations with foreign contractors and Slovak engineering companies, these (Slovak contractors) are not sufficiently competitive mainly as concerns price and delivery schedules," he said.
"This is an unpleasant surprise, but probably the main cause is the low productivity of labour in many Slovak companies," he said.
Slovnaft shares are rated buy despite the company's weaker performance so far this year, a recent investor report issued by the Investmentbank Austria of the Bank Austria Group, said.
"We recommend buying Slovnaft shares.... this is a well run company whose management have the ability and the incentive to deliver strong profits growth" the bank's report said.
